summary: No new receipt this turn, so I used it to close the remaining unexamined durability path and to record the bounded repair picture. The source review of the file snapshot store found no defect: the CRC64 is computed over the written state stream and verified on open, buffered contents are finalized before the metadata is written, and the directory is renamed into place with a parent-directory fsync on non-Windows hosts, so nothing there weakens or contradicts the findings and no claim is made about it. I then added a second durable Fact to the record: a configuration a node holds only in its log can be restored to its in-memory state by exactly three paths — a later configuration entry replicated by a correctly configured leader, an installed snapshot, or a restart with the flag disabled — and where every voter restarts with the flag and no covering snapshot, the first two need a leader that the empty configuration prevents from being elected, so the cluster stays unavailable until an operator acts. That statement cites the executed receipts for both directions (the repair holding at index 5 of 6d6abaf163524e64878c6c9810de2461 and the unrepaired simultaneous-restart case at index 1 of 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a) with source anchors in raft.go for both the append and snapshot-install paths.
